label: Redirect plan
body:
Redirect plan

Cutover

Each DaVinci private-label page the Praxera set replaces becomes a redirect to its replacement, so the pairing is not just provenance — it is the redirect table. 134 redirects: 59 website pages and 75 blog posts. The full mapping, old URL to new, is the second column of every page and post row in the ledger.

Two consequences worth stating plainly. The DaVinci originals must be redirected, not deleted, or the inbound links and the search history go with them. And Praxera slugs must stay fixed from here — the redirect table and the audit spreadsheets both point at them.

Redirect coverageCountReading
Website pages59 a DaVinci pl-demo-* page redirects to each
Blog posts75 the whole blog.davincilabs.com/private-label/ group is covered
Praxera pages that are brand new3 the home page and two thank-you pages. No DaVinci original, so no redirect needed — marked new page in the ledger, not counted as a gap
Published DaVinci pages with nowhere to point 3 the guide landing pages — the one real gap

Three published guide pages have no Praxera equivalent

info.davincilabs.com/private-label-supplements-guide (57 assets link to it), /private-label-supplements-resource-center (14) and /private-label-supplements-client-onboarding (2). Live lead-gen pages with nothing to redirect to, so at cutover they either keep serving DaVinci content or break 73 inbound links.

This is the same gap from the other side as the orphaned forms: Praxera - Supplements Guide, Praxera - Client Onboarding Guide and Praxera - Ingredients & Testing Guide are built and sitting on no page. Building the three Praxera guide pages places those forms and creates the redirect targets in one move.

label: What the re-check changed
body:
What the re-check changed

This version

The whole portal was re-read for this version rather than carried forward from the last one. Six figures moved, and two of the moves matter.

FigureWasIsWhy
Praxera website pages6562 counted against the domain; there are no Praxera landing pages, only site pages
Emails with a clickable DaVinci link0 85 the earlier pass matched hostnames. The footer social icons point at twitter.com/Davincilabsvt and instagram.com/davincilaboratories — the brand is in the path, not the host, so it was missed
Clones enrolling on a DaVinci form— 7 not previously measured. Enrolment was read from the criteria block rather than assumed from the clone log
Dead workflow-list clauses723 the earlier count covered one flow’s worth
Pages with manufacturing claims46 25 the earlier pattern matched across list punctuation, so “we offer: doctor-formulated” read as a claim
Literal “None” on pages260 fixed since the last version; 3 blog posts still carry it

What did not move

Zero published pages, zero published posts, zero sent emails, zero enabled workflows. All 94 workflow email sends still point at a Praxera email, and no DaVinci form is embedded on any Praxera page.

Nothing belonging to another brand was touched. All 486 PetTechLabs, VetriScience and Pet Naturals records — pages, posts, emails and forms, published copy and drafts — were searched: none contains the word Praxera. There is also no structural connection between the two sites: all 62 Praxera pages render from Private Label/Templates/Page - DND.html, PetTechLabs from its own Pet_Tech_Labs templates, and the two sets share zero modules. Some PetTechLabs records do show recent edits on the same HubSpot login this work uses, because the API token is bound to a QBS user account rather than to this project; reading those revisions shows schema markup and internal-linking changes from separate SEO work.

The 16 modules the Praxera pages do share are shared only with unpublished DaVinci pl-demo pages, so the pending global-module edits cannot change a live page.

label: Open items
body:
Open items

Severity ordered — the first four block cutover

Manufacturing claims — 25 pages, 10 posts, 9 emails

Praxera cannot present itself as the manufacturer. Verbatim, from the rendered drafts: “everything we produce is doctor-formulated” (16 assets), “we are one of the most trusted dietary supplement manufacturers” (6), “we handle formulation, manufacturing…”. Provenance wording — “Manufactured in Vermont, U.S.A.” — is fine; the first person is not. The largest remaining item and the only compliance risk.

Three published guide pages have nothing to redirect to

73 assets link to them, 57 to the Supplements Guide alone. Building the three Praxera guide pages also places three of the six orphaned forms.

85 emails link to DaVinci’s social accounts

The footer icon row was cloned intact, so a Praxera email’s Instagram icon opens instagram.com/davincilaboratories and its X icon opens twitter.com/Davincilabsvt. One shared module, so one edit repeated.

7 workflow clones still enrol on a DaVinci form

Five enrol on Contact Us NEW, which has no Praxera clone; one on a deleted form; one on Brand Development Call (Inactive).

Five hidden image descriptions

Invisible on the page, read by screen readers and search engines. Includes the last DaVinci reference on the site and four prexera misspellings. Minutes to fix.

6 pages still carry a clickable DaVinci link

resources and learning/definitive-guide hold most of them. The redirects will catch these after cutover, but a link that needs a redirect to reach the right brand is still worth repointing directly.

Placeholder copy on 11 pages

Nine are marked for Justin or Patrick. The privacy policy still contains [BRAND_TBD] in its body. book-consultation has neither a form nor a booking widget.

Sending identity

108 of 111 clones still reply to enews@davincilabs.com. Praxera needs its own sending domain authenticated before any of this can send.

Blog housekeeping and the domain root

74 of 75 posts carry publish date 1970-01-01, none has tags, and the original CTAs did not survive the clone. 129 blog links still point at praxerasupplements.com/ and nothing is there yet.

53 pages and 107 emails load assets from the DaVinci domain

Not a branding defect — Praxera artwork living in the portal’s file domain. Listed because they break if that domain is disconnected at cutover.

label: Order of operations
body:
Order of operations

The cutover sequence — the last two steps are the irreversible ones

  1. The manufacturing-claim copy pass across 25 pages, 10 posts and 9 emails. The only compliance risk; nothing else should start first.
  2. Build the three Praxera guide pages — places three orphaned forms and closes the redirect gap.
  3. Fix the five image descriptions — minutes, and it removes the last DaVinci reference on the site.
  4. Decide the Praxera social accounts, then fix the shared email footer once.
  5. Point the 7 enrolment triggers at Praxera forms.
  6. Repoint the remaining DaVinci links and edit the shared Product Guide module.
  7. Place the remaining orphaned forms and give book-consultation a booking widget.
  8. Fill the 11 placeholder pages and replace [BRAND_TBD] in the privacy policy.
  9. Authenticate the Praxera sending domain and repoint reply-to.
  10. Stand up the home page at the domain root.
  11. Blog housekeeping — dates, tags, CTAs.
  12. Delete the 23 dead suppression clauses and decide on the D4HCP flow.
  13. Cutover: publish, enable the 12 workflows, switch the originals off, put the 134 redirects in place. Rolling back is doing those in reverse, which is why the originals are redirected rather than deleted.

label: How the asset set was identified
body:
How the asset set was identified

Provenance

Source: HubSpot portal 4087538, read through the CMS, Marketing and Automation v4 APIs on 31 August 2026. Every figure on this page was produced by that pass, not carried forward from an earlier version. Two things about how it was read matter, because they are where an audit of this portal goes wrong:

  • Drafts, not published records. All of this work lives in drafts, so the /draft record is the only one that shows it. Reading the base record shows the site as it was before the migration started — which is how an earlier pass concluded that no Praxera page carried a Praxera form.
  • Whole records, not filtered fields. Passing a property filter to the CMS list endpoints silently drops slug and url, which returns an empty result set that looks like a finding.

Classified by address, not by topic. DaVinci sells supplements under its own name to practitioners and runs a private-label business, from one portal, on one contact list, and the phrase “private label” appears on both sides. PetTechLabs, a separate brand in the same portal, runs its own private-label pet line. So nothing was classified by what it is about — it was classified by the address it lives at: the /private-label/ blog group, an info.davincilabs.com/private-label* slug, the pl-demo-* pages.

The first pass matched the string private-label anywhere in an email and returned 394 hits. Requiring an actual <a href> pointing at a private-label URL — rather than the token appearing in an image filename or a CSS class — drops that to 184. Patrick’s June audit, using different instruments eight weeks earlier, found 183. They agree on 179.

Twenty-five posts are about private label but sit in PetTechLabs’ namespace. Topically they qualify; structurally they are another brand’s, and none was moved.

The scripts that produced these counts are in the project repository, so any figure here can be re-run against the portal and checked rather than taken on trust.
